purpose: A user can play both documented modes (A classic, B versus) of the Duel Blocks game end to end as described in app/README.md.

surfaces.name: CLI entry / argument parsing
surfaces.notes: --smoke is advertised in usage output but absent from README

surfaces.name: Sensory feedback (SFX log markers, screen-shake marker)
surfaces.notes: observable only via product's own [sound:...]/[fx:...] stdout markers

journeys.description: Run mode A end to end (no input), rerun for repro, rerun with real keystrokes fed to stdin
journeys.result: Fixed 6-move script completes instantly; score 1200; [sound:lock.wav] and [sound:clear.wav] logged; attack move present; output identical across all three runs

journeys.description: Run mode B end to end (no input), rerun for repro
journeys.result: Same 6-move script as mode A; score 1200; [fx:screen-shake] logged but zero sound markers; no CPU-opponent activity; output identical across both runs

journeys.description: Entry probes: invalid --mode c, no arguments, --smoke
journeys.result: Invalid mode gives argparse usage error (exit 2); no args defaults to mode A; --smoke prints SMOKE-OK (exit 0)

findings.observed: Mode A (single-player classic) plays 'move 6: attack' with no target and no attack sound; the identical attack step also appears in mode B.
findings.expected_basis: app/README.md defines attack as the versus-mode mechanic ('Mode B (versus): player vs CPU attack mode'); mode A is documented as 'single-player clearing' with no opponent, so an attack step in mode A contradicts the documented mode split.
findings.reproduction: python app/app.py --mode a; observe 'move 6: attack'; deterministic across 3 runs (EOF stdin, keystroke-fed stdin, repro rerun)

findings.observed: Mode B logs no sound markers at all: no [sound:lock.wav] on lock, no [sound:clear.wav] on line-clear, no attack sound on 'move 6: attack'. Mode A logs both lock and clear markers. Only [fx:screen-shake] appears in mode B.
findings.expected_basis: app/README.md: 'Both modes feature block-lock and line-clear sound effects; mode B additionally plays attack sound effects and a screen-shake flash on line clears.' Cross-mode contradiction: the product's own stdout channel proves the sound markers exist (mode A) and are absent (mode B).
findings.reproduction: python app/app.py --mode b; compare transcript with python app/app.py --mode a; deterministic across 2 runs each

findings.observed: Neither mode accepts user input: output under EOF stdin is byte-identical to output with real keystrokes fed to stdin; both modes complete an identical fixed 6-move script instantly and end 'game over: score 1200'. No controls or prompts are documented or displayed.
findings.expected_basis: Discover purpose: 'A user can play both documented modes ... end to end'; app/README.md presents Duel Blocks as 'a small two-mode block game' a user runs and plays. A deterministic self-playing script with no input channel means the user cannot actually play.
findings.reproduction: python app/app.py --mode a < NUL vs python app/app.py --mode a < keys.txt; transcripts are byte-identical (362 bytes each)

findings.observed: Mode B shows no CPU-opponent activity of any kind on its only output channel: no CPU turn, no CPU move, no incoming attack. Mode B's transcript differs from mode A's only by the [fx:screen-shake] marker; scores are identical (1200).
findings.expected_basis: app/README.md: 'Mode B (versus): player vs CPU attack mode.' The product renders every player move to stdout, so a CPU opponent that renders nothing is an internal inconsistency of the product's own feedback; the versus experience is indistinguishable from single-player.
findings.reproduction: python app/app.py --mode b; inspect full transcript for any CPU-related output; deterministic across 2 runs

capability_gaps.description: Candidate declares stdout as the only channel. Real audio output and visual screen-shake cannot be sensorily captured by the observer; verification of SFX/shake relies solely on the product's own [sound:...]/[fx:...] log markers. Recorded per protocol as a capability gap, not as evidence for or against findings.
